findings.reason: the followup is what a coordinator executes, so left as written it schedules §12 ahead of the §14 that shares `resources.py` and re-measures §6 on a tree missing §14, the fix §6 says changes the very read path it measures.
findings.text: f-araiid-009 is the open followup that routes §6's re-measurement ("then re-measure §6"), yet its body still says "§6 is re-measured once all five land" and orders "§12 (the audit's walk) follows §8 and §10", both omitting §14 — which §6's deliverable now lists among those that must be promoted first and which §14 itself places before §12 because both write `resources.py`

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `health-tool-latency/scripts/profile_reads.py` resolves under the health-review-1010 directory §1 names, and the profiler's entrypoints exist (`_roadmap` `reckon/mcp.py:1384`, `_audit` `reckon/mcp.py:2355`, `_discover_project` `reckon/mcp_discovery.py:149`); the docstring's staging is accurate, each invocation producing one cold and one warm sample.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §6's done-when states numeric medians (warm roadmap <= 2 s, warm audit <= 3 s, cold roadmap under the 30 s MCP deadline) and names its negative control, the base revision measured the same way in the same session, which must exceed the deadline for the comparison to count.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate log lands under the run directory and the `.prof` dumps under the run's report directory, both durable crew-run paths rather than a node-local temporary tree.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §6 carries no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and no changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §6 is a measurement node with no mechanism of its own; its premise that the listed fixes move the reads inside the deadline matches §7's and §9's attribution, and it names the tool it runs and the MCP caller it relies on.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §6 carries one deliverable, the deadline measurement of the three reads after the fixes land.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §6's deliverable now names §14 among the fixes it runs after, but f-araiid-009, the open followup that routes §6's re-measurement, still recounts §6's prerequisites as "all five" and orders §12 only after §8 and §10, omitting §14.
